title: VF-MT301-FleetDesiredStateSchema
clause: PostgreSQL desired-state schema + typed Rust rows for the microVM workspace fleet (Running/Snapshotted/Absent, resource budgets, priority), NOTIFY wake-up wiring on binding/lease/desired-state writes, typed EventLedger events for desired-state changes

scope.summary:
GOAL: Give the microVM workspace fleet a durable, PostgreSQL-authoritative DESIRED-STATE layer that the MT-302 reconciler daemon can diff against OBSERVED state. Today the WP-1 primitives record only observed/ownership state: worktree_vm_bindings (migration 0365_worktree_vm_bindings.sql lines 8-30) stores binding_state IN ('active','snapshotted','terminated','failed') with a generation BIGINT fencing column (line 15, incremented at worktree_vm_registry.rs persist_handle_in_transaction ~line 1077 'generation = worktree_vm_bindings.generation + 1'), and ModelLane rows carry heartbeat_at_utc / lease_expires_at_utc / reclaim_after_utc / restart_generation (model_lane.rs lines 6571-6574, monotonic restart_generation enforcement ~lines 5832-5851). Nothing anywhere says what the fleet SHOULD look like. This MT adds: (1) a worktree_fleet_desired_state table with per-worktree desired workspace state (Running / Snapshotted / Absent), resource budget (memory MiB, vcpus), and scheduling priority; (2) LISTEN/NOTIFY wake-up wiring (trigger functions) on desired-state writes, worktree_vm_bindings writes, and lease writes, carrying a key-only hint payload (research P7: NOTIFY is a hint, never a queue - the reconciler always re-reads full rows); (3) typed EventLedger events for every desired-state change so fleet intent is replayable; (4) typed Rust rows + a scope-enforcing store module. All Rust, PostgreSQL/EventLedger authority only, NO SQLite anywhere, no Kubernetes/Docker/containerd/Nomad dependencies (heuristics only, per the recorded research basis), no new external daemons.

RESOURCE PRIVACY: fleet rows are account/Principal-scoped exactly like worktree_vm_bindings. The table carries owner_account_id, actor_principal_id, authenticated_session_id, access_space_id, workspace_id columns matching resource_scope.rs (OwnerAccountId line 53, ActorPrincipalId line 60, AuthenticatedSessionRef line 67, AccessSpaceRef line 73, WorkspaceScopeRef line 117, ResourceScope struct lines 147-153) and the store re-authorizes every deserialized row via stored_resource_scope_from_row + an exact-scope check, mirroring WorktreeVmDurableStore::require_scope (worktree_vm_registry.rs lines 1004-1019) and its load path (lines 1164-1207). The table is registered in model_lane_resource_scope_registry exactly as migration 0365 does at lines 38-40.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: one new migration pair (allocate the next free migration number in the implementing worktree at implementation time; numbering >= 0366 since 0365 is taken on the WP-1 branch), a new module src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/vm_fleet/desired_state.rs (module dir vm_fleet/ with mod.rs registered from swarm_orchestration/mod.rs), typed EventLedger event constructors, and tests. No edits to worktree_vm_registry.rs semantics; only additive triggers on its table.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Migration NNNN_vm_fleet_desired_state.sql (name final; number allocated at implementation):
   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS worktree_fleet_desired_state (
       desired_id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
       worktree_id TEXT NOT NULL,
       desired_state TEXT NOT NULL,
       memory_budget_mib INTEGER NOT NULL,
       vcpu_budget INTEGER NOT NULL,
       priority INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
       desired_generation BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
       owner_account_id UUID NOT NULL,
       actor_principal_id UUID NOT NULL,
       authenticated_session_id UUID NOT NULL,
       access_space_id UUID NOT NULL,
       workspace_id TEXT NOT NULL,
       created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
       updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
       CONSTRAINT chk_fleet_desired_worktree CHECK (length(btrim(worktree_id)) > 0),
       CONSTRAINT chk_fleet_desired_state CHECK (desired_state IN ('running','snapshotted','absent')),
       CONSTRAINT chk_fleet_desired_memory CHECK (memory_budget_mib > 0),
       CONSTRAINT chk_fleet_desired_vcpu CHECK (vcpu_budget > 0),
       CONSTRAINT uq_fleet_desired_scope UNIQUE (owner_account_id, workspace_id, worktree_id)
   );
   plus indexes (owner_account_id, workspace_id, desired_state) and (actor_principal_id), plus INSERT INTO model_lane_resource_scope_registry (table_name) VALUES ('worktree_fleet_desired_state') ON CONFLICT (table_name) DO NOTHING; matching 0365 lines 32-40. Provide the .down.sql twin.
2. NOTIFY wiring (same migration): one trigger function hsk_vm_fleet_notify() RETURNS trigger that executes pg_notify('hsk_vm_fleet_changed', payload) where payload is a compact JSON hint {"worktree_id": ..., "owner_account_id": ..., "workspace_id": ..., "source_table": TG_TABLE_NAME} and NOTHING else - no state, no action verbs (research P6/P7: level-triggered core, edge-triggered wake-up; a lost NOTIFY must never lose work because the resync tick re-reads everything). Attach AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE triggers to worktree_fleet_desired_state AND worktree_vm_bindings. For lease writes: the WP-1 lease surface is EventLedger-backed ModelLane state (NewModelLaneLease, model_lane.rs lines 8129-8148; ModelLaneLeaseRecord lines 8151-8158) rather than a bespoke lease table; wire the notify into the fleet store's own Rust write path for lease-affecting fleet operations (store emits pg_notify on the same channel after commit) and document in code why the trigger cannot sit on a ledger-internal table. If the implementing worktree exposes a physical lease/heartbeat table for lanes, attach the same trigger there instead; decide from the code, not from this contract.
3. Typed Rust rows (vm_fleet/desired_state.rs):
   pub enum FleetDesiredState { Running, Snapshotted, Absent } with as_str()/parse() exactly in the WorktreeVmBindingState style (worktree_vm_registry.rs lines 106-140), serde snake_case, parse failure = typed error (never a panic, never a silent default).
   pub struct FleetResourceBudget { pub memory_mib: i32, pub vcpus: i32 }
   pub struct FleetDesiredStateRecord { pub desired_id: Uuid, pub worktree_id: String, pub desired_state: FleetDesiredState, pub budget: FleetResourceBudget, pub priority: i32, pub desired_generation: i64 }
   pub struct FleetDesiredStateStore { pool: PgPool, access: ResourceAccessContext } with:
   pub async fn upsert_desired(&self, worktree_id: &str, desired: FleetDesiredState, budget: FleetResourceBudget, priority: i32) -> Result<FleetDesiredStateRecord, FleetDesiredStateError>  // ON CONFLICT (owner_account_id, workspace_id, worktree_id) DO UPDATE ... desired_generation = worktree_fleet_desired_state.desired_generation + 1, guarded by the same exact-scope WHERE predicate shape as persist_handle_in_transaction (worktree_vm_registry.rs lines 1058-1096)
   pub async fn load_desired(&self, worktree_id: &str) -> Result<Option<FleetDesiredStateRecord>, FleetDesiredStateError>
   pub async fn list_desired(&self) -> Result<Vec<FleetDesiredStateRecord>, FleetDesiredStateError>  // scope-filtered in SQL AND re-authorized per row after deserialization
   pub async fn remove_desired(&self, worktree_id: &str) -> ...  // sets desired_state='absent', never DELETEs (row removal is MT-305 finalizer territory)
4. EventLedger events: typed constructors for FLEET_DESIRED_STATE_SET / FLEET_DESIRED_STATE_CLEARED appended through the existing EventLedger write path used by ModelLane records (model_lane.rs event_ledger_stream_id / event_ledger_seq / event_stream_version fields, e.g. lines 8140 and 8154-8157), payload = { worktree_id, desired_state, memory_budget_mib, vcpu_budget, priority, desired_generation }. Ledger append and row upsert commit in the same transaction where the existing ledger API permits; otherwise ledger-first with the row write carrying the ledger event id, and a code comment stating which ordering was possible and why.
5. HOUSE RULES baked in: no SQLite (PostgreSQL only), no Kubernetes/Docker/containerd/Nomad crates or daemons, no new external daemons, disk-agnostic paths only (no absolute paths, no drive letters), no file or folder names with spaces, all proof commands run with per-owner scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR under the external artifacts root ../Handshake_Artifacts/.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read worktree_vm_registry.rs lines 1-200 (error/state/record types) and 1003-1310 (WorktreeVmDurableStore scope + SQL shapes), migration 0365 in full, resource_scope.rs in full, and the current highest migration number in the implementing worktree.
2. Write the migration + .down.sql with the table, constraints, indexes, notify trigger function, triggers, and resource-scope registry insert.
3. Create vm_fleet/mod.rs + vm_fleet/desired_state.rs with the enums, records, error type, and FleetDesiredStateStore; register vm_fleet in swarm_orchestration/mod.rs.
4. Wire the EventLedger typed events for desired-state changes.
5. Write tests against real PostgreSQL (Spec-Realism Gate: fixture-only proof is insufficient): upsert bumps desired_generation; cross-account row invisible; cross-workspace row invisible; scope-mismatched upsert affects zero rows; NOTIFY fires on desired-state write and on a worktree_vm_bindings write (LISTEN in test, assert hint payload has key fields only); parse() rejects unknown desired_state.
6. Run proof targets; record measured output. Implementer never marks COMPLETED - the WP validator advances the verdict.

acceptance_criteria: AC-301-1: Migration creates worktree_fleet_desired_state with desired_state CHECK IN ('running','snapshotted','absent'), memory_budget_mib > 0, vcpu_budget > 0, priority, desired_generation BIGINT DEFAULT 1, full five-column resource scope, UNIQUE (owner_account_id, workspace_id, worktree_id), and registers the table in model_lane_resource_scope_registry; a .down.sql twin reverses it.
AC-301-2: FleetDesiredState { Running, Snapshotted, Absent } is serde snake_case with as_str()/parse(); parse() of an unknown value returns a typed error proven by test.

AC-301-3: FleetDesiredStateStore::upsert_desired increments desired_generation on conflict and its UPDATE is guarded by the exact-scope predicate; a live PostgreSQL test proves a scope-mismatched upsert affects zero rows and surfaces a typed scope error.

AC-301-4: All store reads are scope-filtered in SQL and re-authorized per row after deserialization (stored_resource_scope_from_row + exact-scope check); a live test proves a second account cannot read or enumerate the first account's fleet rows.

AC-301-5: pg_notify('hsk_vm_fleet_changed', ...) fires on writes to worktree_fleet_desired_state and worktree_vm_bindings; the payload carries only identifying hint fields (worktree_id, owner_account_id, workspace_id, source_table) and no actionable state - proven by a LISTEN-based live test.

AC-301-6: Every desired-state change appends a typed EventLedger event (FLEET_DESIRED_STATE_SET / FLEET_DESIRED_STATE_CLEARED) carrying worktree_id, desired_state, budgets, priority, desired_generation.
AC-301-7: remove_desired writes desired_state='absent' and never issues a SQL DELETE against the fleet table; grep proof target confirms no DELETE FROM worktree_fleet_desired_state in the module.
AC-301-8: Zero SQLite, Kubernetes, Docker, containerd, or Nomad dependencies introduced; proof target greps Cargo.toml and the new module for the forbidden identifiers.
AC-301-9: Proof commands run with per-owner scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR under ../Handshake_Artifacts/ and tests execute against a real PostgreSQL database (Spec-Realism Gate), not fixtures only.

implementation_notes: IMPLEMENTATION GATE: do not start until WP-1 Integration Validator batch verdicts return and the WP-1 feature branch merges to main - the primitives this MT builds on (worktree_vm_bindings, resource_scope, ledger types) live on that branch (frozen candidate df463aa6). See expansion_provenance.implementation_gate.
NOTIFY is a wake-up hint only (research P7): nothing in the payload may be treated as a work item; the MT-302 reconciler re-reads full rows on every pass. Do not add payload fields 'to be helpful'.
Never DELETE fleet rows here: Absent is a desired state the reconciler converges to; physical row lifecycle (tombstones) belongs to MT-305.

Migration numbering: 0365 is the highest verified fleet-relevant number on the WP-1 branch; allocate the actual next free number in the implementing worktree at implementation time and keep the descriptive suffix vm_fleet_desired_state.
Disk-agnostic discipline: no absolute paths, no drive letters, no user-profile paths anywhere in code, SQL, or tests; artifacts root is the relative ../Handshake_Artifacts/.
Implementer never marks COMPLETED; lifecycle advancement is the WP validator's verdict.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Schema/store MT; the operator-facing fleet surface is MT-306. Desired-state intent is reconstructable from the typed EventLedger events this MT adds.

target_entries: Workspace fleet > Desired state model (Running / Snapshotted / Absent, budgets, priority)
Workspace fleet > How fleet intent is recorded (EventLedger events, NOTIFY wake-up channel)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: Desired-state changes are ledger events in this MT; FR reconcile-pass events land in MT-306. Record DEFERRED-to-MT-306 if no FR emission point exists yet.
Emit a diagnostic event on desired-state write failure (scope mismatch, constraint violation) via the open diagnostic-event API if present; otherwise DEFERRED-with-reason.
Pure schema/store MT with no long-lived process; liveness capture adds no evidence beyond PostgreSQL state and ledger events.

risk_if_missed: The reconciler family has no desired-state source of truth: MT-302..305 would have to infer intent from observed bindings, which is exactly the edge-triggered anti-pattern the research basis rejects, and fleet intent would be unreplayable and unscoped.

risks: RISK-1: NOTIFY payload grows actionable state and a consumer acts on it directly, so a dropped notification (disconnect, PgBouncer transaction pooling) silently loses a fleet action.
RISK-2: Fleet rows written without the exact five-column resource scope leak one account's workspace topology to another account or to an unscoped reader.
RISK-3: A DELETE-based remove path erases desired state before the reconciler converges, orphaning a live VM with no record of what it should become.
RISK-4: desired_generation is not bumped on upsert, so MT-303 generation fencing cannot reject stale reconcile plans built against superseded intent.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Trigger function emits key-only hint payload; AC-301-5 live test asserts payload fields; MT-302 contract independently forbids payload-driven action.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): NOT NULL scope columns + UNIQUE scope key + per-row post-deserialization re-authorization; AC-301-4 cross-account live test.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): remove_desired writes 'absent', never DELETE; AC-301-7 grep proof plus code review.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE always sets desired_generation = desired_generation + 1; AC-301-3 live test proves the bump.
